$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[lem-gr-tensor-bundle-coordinate-construction]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] to change slot variance.
For example, if $T$ is a type $(1,1)$ field, lowering its contravariant slot
gives the type $(0,2)$ field with components $T_{ab}:=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$; if $S$
is a type $(0,2)$ field, raising its first covariant slot gives the type
$(1,1)$ field with components $S^a{}_b:=g^{ac}S_{cb}$. Each operation changes
the tensor type and is invertible because $g_p$ is nondegenerate.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[lem-gr-tensor-bundle-coordinate-construction]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

Let $n\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let

$$A:I\longrightarrow M_n(\mathbb R),\qquad A(t)=\bigl(a_{ij}(t)\bigr),$$

be a matrix-valued curve whose entries $a_{ij}:I\to\mathbb R$ are differentiable at $t_0\in I$ ([[def-derivative]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); write $A'(t_0):=\bigl(a_{ij}'(t_0)\bigr)$ ([[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Suppose $A(t)$ is invertible for every $t\in I$ ([[thm-real-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-nonzero]], [[cor-inverse-matrix-by-adjugate]]). Then $t\mapsto\det A(t)$ is differentiable at $t_0$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]) and

$$(\det A)'(t_0)=\det A(t_0)\;\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(A(t_0)^{-1}A'(t_0)\bigr),$$

with the trace of [[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]. In particular, a $C^1$ matrix curve with invertible values has $(\det A)'=\det A\,\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}A')$ on all of $I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), so that at every $p\in M$ the form
$g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$, and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) whose
support is compact.

**(a) Pointwise openness.** Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $4$
and let $G$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$ of inertia $(3,1,0)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). If in some basis of $V$ the matrix of $G$
has the form $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)+E$, then $G$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$
whenever $|E_{ij}|<1/8$ for all $i,j$. Consequently, for every basis the set
of matrices of symmetric forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$ is open in the space
$M_4^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ with respect to the maximum-entry norm, and
equivalently $g_p$ has a neighborhood in the space of symmetric forms at $p$
consisting entirely of forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$.

**(b) Global stability.** There is $\lambda_0>0$ such that for every real
$\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the smooth symmetric field $g+\lambda h$
is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with
time orientation inherited from $N$ (the field $N$ remains timelike for
$g+\lambda h$ for $|\lambda|$ small).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.
Every continuous real function on a closed nondegenerate rectangle $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge1$, is Riemann integrable.

For a bounded function $f:Q\to\mathbb R$ on a nondegenerate rectangle
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, define
$$\underline{\int_Q}f:=\sup_P L(f,P),\qquad \overline{\int_Q}f:=\inf_P U(f,P),$$
over all grid partitions $P$ of $Q$. The grid family is nonempty, since the endpoints in each coordinate give a one-cell grid. Every lower sum is at most every upper sum by a common refinement and [[lem-multidimensional-refinement-inequalities]], so the two sets of sums are nonempty and bounded and the extrema exist ([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[thm-infimum-property]], [[def-infimum]], [[lem-sup-unique]]).

The function is **Riemann integrable over $Q$** when the two values agree.
Their unique common real is $\int_Q f$. No integral is defined here for a
degenerate rectangle, because the grid definition requires every coordinate
interval to have distinct endpoints. This is the multidimensional Darboux
definition; its agreement with the published one-dimensional definition is
proved separately.

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ and $B\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ be nondegenerate closed rectangles, and let $f:A\times B\to\mathbb R$ be Riemann integrable. Then the four lower and upper section-integral functions of [[def-sections-and-iterated-riemann-integrals]] are Riemann integrable and
$$\int_A\ell_B=\int_Au_B=\int_{A\times B}f=\int_B\ell_A=\int_Bu_A.$$

If the $B$-sections are integrable outside a content-zero set $N\subseteq A$, every bounded exceptionally completed function $h$ with $h(x)=\int_Bf_x$ for $x\notin N$ is integrable and
$$\int_{A\times B}f=\int_Ah.$$
The same assertion holds with the coordinate blocks exchanged. In particular, when every section in an order is integrable, the ordinary iterated integral in that order exists and equals the multiple integral. The theorem does not assert that every section of an integrable function is integrable.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Let $(X,d_X)$ be a compact metric space ([[def-metric-compactness]]), let
$(Y,d_Y)$ be any metric space ([[def-metric-space]]) and let $f : X \to Y$ be
continuous ([[def-metric-continuity]]). Then $f$ is uniformly continuous
([[def-metric-uniform-continuity]]).

No choice principle is used: the cover built below is cut out by a property, and
the Lebesgue number lemma it is fed to is itself choice free
([[thm-lebesgue-number-lemma]]).

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Let $f:Q\to\mathbb R$ be bounded on a nondegenerate rectangle and let $P$ be a grid. For each cell $Q_i$, put
$$m_i:=\inf f[Q_i],\quad M_i:=\sup f[Q_i],\quad L(f,P):=\sum_i m_i\operatorname{vol}(Q_i),\quad U(f,P):=\sum_i M_i\operatorname{vol}(Q_i).$$
The extrema exist as finite reals because each nonempty image is bounded ([[def-bounded-set]], [[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[thm-infimum-property]], [[def-infimum]], [[lem-sup-unique]]), and the sums use the iterated convention of [[def-multidimensional-grid-partition]].

Since $m_i\le M_i$ and cell volumes are nonnegative, $L(f,P)\le U(f,P)$. Moreover
$$U(f,P)-L(f,P)=\sum_i(M_i-m_i)\operatorname{vol}(Q_i),$$
the sum of cell oscillations weighted by volume ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $a<b$, and
let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve whose image is
contained in the domain $U$ of one smooth chart $(U,x)$
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Suppose $\gamma$ is
parametrized so that

$$g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)=-c^2 \qquad (t\in[a,b]),$$

that is, by proper time up to a choice of origin
([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). Let
$H:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times[a,b]\to U$ be a map that is $C^2$ in both
variables, with $H(0,t)=\gamma(t)$ for all $t$, with
$H(s,a)=\gamma(a)$ and $H(s,b)=\gamma(b)$ for all $s$, and such that each
curve $t\mapsto H(s,t)$ is future timelike; write
$T(s,t):=\partial_tH(s,t)$, $J(t):=\partial_sH(s,t)|_{s=0}$, so that
$J(a)=J(b)=0$, and

$$L(s):=\int_a^b\sqrt{-g_{H(s,t)}\bigl(T(s,t),T(s,t)\bigr)}\,dt .$$

Then:

1. $L$ is differentiable at $0$ and
   $$L'(0)=-\int_a^b\frac{g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tJ(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}}\,dt =-\frac1c\int_a^bg_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tJ(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)\,dt .$$
2. Equivalently,
   $L'(0)=\frac1c\int_a^bg_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(J(t),D_t\gamma'(t)\bigr)\,dt$.
3. $L'(0)=0$ for **every** such variation $H$ if and only if
   $D_t\gamma'=0$ on $[a,b]$. Consequently, within this class, stationarity
   of the length functional is exactly the geodesic equation in the given
   proper-time parameter.

The chart hypothesis is used to realize variations of prescribed compactly
supported variation fields by coordinate displacement; the formula of claim 1
and the implication "geodesic $\Rightarrow$ stationary" are local and do not
require it beyond the smooth parametrization.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation
$[f]\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(t)$ on smooth germs at $\gamma(t)$, extending
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] from smooth to $C^1$ curves.
Equal germ representatives agree along the curve near $t$, and the
one-variable product rule proves the derivation identity. In a chart around
$\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** For $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$,
a **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

derivations.claim: (Variation of the inverse metric.) Differentiate the identity $g(s)^{ac}g(s)_{cb}=\delta^{a}{}_{b}$ at $s=0$ using [L5]: $q^{ac}g_{cb}+g^{ac}h_{cb}=0$. Multiplying by $g^{-1}$ twice gives $q^{ab}=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$, the first assertion of (a).

(Variation of the Christoffel symbols.) Fix $p$, use the point-normal chart of [L2] at $p$, and let $g(s)$ be the given family; at $p$, the Christoffel formula of [L1] applied to $g(s)$ gives $\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}(p)=	frac12g(s)^{ad}(p) igl(\partial_bg(s)_{dc}+\partial_cg(s)_{bd}-\partial_dg(s)_{bc} igr)(p)$. Differentiating at $s=0$ and using $g(0)=g$, the derivatives of the metric at $p$ may be replaced by covariant derivatives because $\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}(p)=0$; this gives $\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}(p)=	frac12g^{ad}(
abla_bh_{cd}+
abla_ch_{bd}-
abla_dh_{bc})(p)$, the displayed formula. Both sides are tensor fields: the left side is a difference of Christoffel-symbol families, whose transformation law differs only by a metric-independent term that cancels, and the right side is built from tensors. Since the identity holds at every point in some point-normal chart, it holds on $U$; this proves (b).

(Realizability.) Let $h_0$ be smooth symmetric with compact support in $U$. By [L6] applied to the Lorentzian metric $g$ and the field $h_0$, there is $\lambda_0>0$ such that $g+\mu h_0$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $|\mu|<\lambda_0$. For $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ and $|s|<1$ put $g(s):=g+s\lambda h_0$, so that $\mu=s\lambda$ ranges over $(-\lambda_0,\lambda_0)$; then $g(s)$ is Lorentzian for every $s\in(-1,1)$, equals $g$ off $K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$, and its components are smooth in $(s,x)$. For an arbitrary prescribed $q$, take $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$ and restrict $g+s h$ to the stability interval; step 1.1 gives exactly that inverse-metric derivative. This proves the remaining assertions of (a).

(Palatini identity.) In the point-normal chart at $p$, the chart expression of [L3] reads $R(s)^{a}{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{cb}+\sum_e igl(\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{ce}\Gamma(s)^{e}{}_{db}-\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{de}\Gamma(s)^{e}{}_{cb} igr)$. At $p$ the quadratic terms have a factor $\Gamma(0)^{e}{}_{xy}(p)=0$, so differentiating at $s=0$ gives $\delta R^{a}{}_{bcd}(p)=\partial_c\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}(p)-\partial_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{cb}(p)=
abla_c\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}(p)-
abla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{cb}(p)$, where the last equality again uses $\Gamma(p)=0$. Both sides are tensors, so the identity holds on $U$. Contracting $a=c$ with [L3], $\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\delta R^{a}{}_{bad}=
abla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-
abla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}$, which is (c).

(Variation of the density times scalar curvature.) From [L4], $\partial_sw(s)|_0=-	frac12w\,g_{ab}q^{ab}$, and from step 1.1 and (c), $\partial_sS(s)|_0=\partial_s(g(s)^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd})|_0=q^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}+g^{bd}\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$. Therefore $$\partial_s igl(w(s)S(s) igr) ig|_0=w\Bigl[\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}q^{bd}-	frac12S\,g_{bd}q^{bd}+g^{bd} igl(
abla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-
abla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab} igr)\Bigr] .$$ The first two terms are $wG_{bd}q^{bd}$ by [L3]. For the last two terms, metric compatibility ($
abla g^{-1}=0$, [L1]) gives $g^{bd}
abla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}=
abla_a(g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db})$ and $g^{bd}
abla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}=
abla_d(g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab})=
abla_a(g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db})$ after relabelling the second index; their difference is $
abla_aV^{a}$ with $V^{a}=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$, so $\partial_s(wS)|_0=wG_{ab}q^{ab}+w
abla_aV^{a}$. Since $\partial_a(wV^a)=w
abla_aV^{a}$ by the density-divergence formula [L7], this is (d).

(Chart integral.) The action-difference integrand $[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)]$ is smooth in $(s,x)$ on $I\times x(U)$ and supported in the fixed compact set $K$; all its $s$-derivatives are supported in $K$. By [L8], $F$ is differentiable at $0$ with $F'(0)=\int_U\partial_s\bigl((S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)\bigr)|_0d^4x$. By [L4] and (d), $\partial_s((S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s))|_0=wG_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^{a})+\Lambda g_{ab}q^{ab}w=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^{a})$, the last step by [L7]. The function $\partial_a(wV^{a})$ has compact support in $K\subseteq U$, so its integral vanishes by [L8]; hence $F'(0)=\int_U(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}w\,d^4x$, which is (e).

(Particle functional.) Clause (f) is exactly [L9]: the lemma's hypotheses are the stated ones, and its conclusions are the formulas (1)-(3) quoted in (f). Multiplying the length functional by the positive constant $mc$ gives $S_p(H(s,\cdot))=-mc\,L(s)$, so $\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_0=-mc\,L'(0)$; since $mc>0$, the vanishing of $L'(0)$ for every admissible variation is equivalent to the vanishing of $\partial_sS_p|_0$, and [L9] identifies this with $D_t\gamma'=0$.

citations.quote: For a covariant $k$-tensor $T=T_{i_1\cdots i_k}dx^{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes dx^{i_k}$, $$ (\mathcal L_XT)_{i_1\cdots i_k}=X^j\partial_jT_{i_1\cdots i_k}+\sum_a(\partial_{i_a}X^j)T_{i_1\cdots j\cdots i_k}. $$

If $X$ has local flow $\Phi_t$ and $T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$, its Lie derivative is $$\mathcal L_XT=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*T,$$ on every local flow domain where this derivative is defined. Here the pullback by the local diffeomorphism $\Phi_t$ acts by $d\Phi_{-t}$ on each contravariant slot and by $d\Phi_t$ on each covariant slot.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $\nabla$ be an affine connection on
$M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) and let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, with Christoffel symbols $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a
\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$ ([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]])
and metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$. Then:

1. $\nabla$ is torsion-free ([[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]])
   if and only if $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\Gamma^a{}_{cb}$ for all $a,b,c$ in every
   smooth chart.
2. $\nabla$ is $g$-compatible ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) if and
   only if, in every smooth chart,

$$\partial_ag_{bc}=\sum_{d=0}^{3}\bigl(\Gamma^d{}_{ab}g_{dc}+\Gamma^d{}_{ac}g_{bd}\bigr) \qquad(a,b,c=0,1,2,3).$$

Thus $\nabla$ is metric-selected for $(M,g)$ if and only if both displayed
conditions hold in every smooth chart.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the
sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] (so that its
charts that are oriented in that orientation have orientation-preserving
transition maps), and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection. This item
fixes the metric volume form, the flux of a current through oriented $3$-faces
and finite-chain charges. The orientation of $M$ is an independent datum: it is
not determined by the metric and not by the time orientation.

**(a) Metric volume density and volume form.** Let $(U,x)$ be an oriented
chart, with metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)). Define the **metric volume
density**

$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a strictly positive smooth function because $g_{ab}$ is smooth and
$g_p$ is nondegenerate. In the chart define the local $4$-form

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}:=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

with the exterior product of [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]] and the
coordinate covector fields of
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. That these local
forms agree on chart overlaps and therefore define one smooth nowhere-vanishing
$4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — is proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (a), together
with the reading statement of clause (b) there: in every oriented chart
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^3$, and on every positively
oriented $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ one has
$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1$.

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a
smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current
$3$-form** of $J$ is the contraction

$$\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

the interior product of the $4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $J$
([[def-interior-product-of-a-form-by-a-vector-field]]).

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-simplex` (differential-geometry track),
restated here so this page is self-contained — we mean a map
$\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ whose domain is the standard $k$-simplex
$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$
for which there exist an open set $O\subseteq A^k=\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\sum_it_i=1\}$
containing $\Delta^k$ and a smooth map $\bar\sigma:O\to M$ with
$\bar\sigma|_{\Delta^k}=\sigma$; the extension is not part of the simplex
data, and degenerate parametrizations are allowed. With the integration of
forms over such simplices
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]]), a **$3$-face** is
a smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$, and the **flux of $J$ through
$\sigma$** is the real number

$$\Phi_J(\sigma):=\int_\sigma\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

A **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes`, restated here —
is a finite formal real linear combination $\Sigma=\sum_i c_i\sigma_i$ of
smooth singular $k$-simplices. For such a $3$-chain the **flux of $J$ through
$\Sigma$** is defined additively,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma):=\sum_i c_i\,\Phi_J(\sigma_i),$$

a definition independent of the written expression for $\Sigma$, because a
finite formal sum is evaluated by adding the finitely many coefficients and
inserting a zero coefficient changes nothing. $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ is the **charge**
of the current $J$ assigned to $\Sigma$ when the model reads $J$ as a conserved
current; that reading belongs to the physical postulates and is not part of
this definition.

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace
$H\subseteq T_pM$ is **nondegenerate** for $g_p$ when the restriction of $g_p$
to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has
dimension $3$ and is nondegenerate at $\sigma(t)$, and **non-null** when this holds at every
parameter point. For a non-null face the **unit normal** $\nu$ at that point is
the unique vector of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$ with $\nu\in H^\perp$,
$g(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $(\nu,\sigma_*\partial_1,\sigma_*\partial_2,
\sigma_*\partial_3)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$; its
existence, uniqueness and its sign $\varepsilon:=g(\nu,\nu)$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c), together
with the density identity of clause (c) used to read $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ on
such a face. Rank-deficient faces and rank-three faces with degenerate induced
metric are not assigned a unit normal; their flux is defined
by the $3$-form $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ itself, as in clause (b).

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold, let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $(U,x)$ be any smooth
chart, with indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$. Write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$,
let $(g^{ab})$ be the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$, and define the strictly
positive chart weight $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$. These are local
matrix constructions; no signature, time orientation or orientation is assumed.
A continuous covariant tensor field means a family of bilinear forms whose
chart components are continuous; smooth means that they are $C^\infty$.
For a covector or vector field the same regularity convention applies to its
components in the coordinate dual basis or coordinate basis, respectively.
Let $F$ be a
continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$. Suppose that for every
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $q$ on $M$ whose support is a
compact subset of $U$,

$$\int_U F_{ab}(x)\,q^{ab}(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0,$$

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a

([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library

$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace

to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has

If $X$ has local flow $\Phi_t$ and $T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$, its Lie derivative is $$\mathcal L_XT=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*T,$$ on every local flow domain where this derivative is defined. Here the pullback by the local diffeomorphism $\Phi_t$ acts by $d\Phi_{-t}$ on each contravariant slot and by $d\Phi_t$ on each covariant slot.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$.

A **local flow** of $X$ consists of an open set $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R\times M$
containing $\{0\}\times M$ and a smooth map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ such that:

1. $\Phi(0,p)=p$ for every $p\in M$;
2. for each $p$, the fibre $\mathcal D_p:=\{t:(t,p)\in\mathcal D\}$ is an
   interval;
3. for each $p$, the curve $t\mapsto \Phi(t,p)$ is an integral curve of $X$ on
   $\mathcal D_p$;
4. whenever both sides are defined,
   $\Phi(t,\Phi(s,p))=\Phi(t+s,p)$.

If $\mathcal D=\mathbb R\times M$, then $\Phi$ is the **global flow** of $X$.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-ordered-field]]) with its order
([[def-real-order]]).

A subset $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is **order-convex** when

$$x, y \in I \text{ and } x \le z \le y \;\Longrightarrow\; z \in I .$$

The **intervals** of $\mathbb{R}$ are the sets of the following nine forms, where
$a, b \in \mathbb{R}$:

| | bounded forms | | one-sided and full forms |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(a,b)$ | $\{x : a < x < b\}$ | $(a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a < x\}$ |
| $[a,b]$ | $\{x : a \le x \le b\}$ | $[a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a \le x\}$ |
| $[a,b)$ | $\{x : a \le x < b\}$ | $(-\infty,b)$ | $\{x : x < b\}$ |
| $(a,b]$ | $\{x : a < x \le b\}$ | $(-\infty,b]$ | $\{x : x \le b\}$ |
| | | $(-\infty,\infty)$ | $\mathbb{R}$ |

An interval is **open** when both of its written endpoints are excluded, that is
for the forms $(a,b)$, $(a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b)$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$; it is
**closed** when both written endpoints are included, that is for $[a,b]$,
$[a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b]$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$. The forms $[a,b)$ and
$(a,b]$ are **half-open**.

**The symbols $\pm\infty$ are notation and not elements of $\mathbb{R}$.** They
mark which side carries no endpoint condition at all; the five forms in the right
column are defined by the displayed conditions on $x$ alone, and no arithmetic is
ever performed with $\infty$. This is the same refusal to extend $\mathbb{R}$
silently that [[rem-sup-conventions]] records for suprema.

**Every one of the nine forms is order-convex.** Each is defined by a conjunction
of at most two conditions, each of the shape $a < x$, $a \le x$, $x < b$ or
$x \le b$, and each such condition is inherited by an intermediate point: if
$a < x$ and $x \le z$ then $a < z$, and if $z \le y$ and $y < b$ then $z < b$,
by transitivity of the order ([[def-ordered-field]]). Applying this to whichever
one or two conditions define the form in question gives $z \in I$ whenever
$x, y \in I$ and $x \le z \le y$.

**Bounded intervals.** An interval is **bounded** ([[def-bounded-set]]) exactly
when it is of one of the four forms in the left column: for those, $a$ is a lower
bound and $b$ an upper bound. The other five forms are unbounded, on the side or
sides written with $\infty$; the verification is in the remarks below.

**Nondegeneracy.** An interval is **degenerate** when it has at most one element,
and **nondegenerate** when it has at least two. For the four bounded forms with
endpoints $a$ and $b$:

- $[a,b]$ is nonempty exactly when $a \le b$, and it is nondegenerate exactly
  when $a < b$. It is the singleton $\{a\}$ when $a = b$.
- $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are nonempty exactly when $a < b$, and then each
  is nondegenerate.

The only assertion here that is not immediate from the defining conditions is
that $a < b$ makes $(a,b)$ nonempty with at least two points. It holds because
$a < (a+b)/2 < b$, which follows from $a < b$ by adding $a$, respectively $b$, to
both sides and halving ([[def-ordered-field]]); repeating the halving inside
$(a, (a+b)/2)$ produces a second point.

**Closed bounded intervals.** These are the sets $[a,b]$ with $a \le b$, which is
exactly the condition making them nonempty. They are the intervals the nested
interval property is stated for, and the phrase *closed bounded interval* always
carries the hypothesis $a \le b$ in this library.

**Length.** The **length** of a bounded interval presented by its endpoints
$a \le b$ is

$$\ell = b - a \;\ge\; 0 .$$

Length is attached to the presentation by endpoints and is not recovered from the
set: $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are all empty when $a = b$, and so is
$(c,c)$ for any other $c$, while each of these presentations has length $0$, so
nothing inconsistent arises; but the endpoints are named explicitly at every
point where a length is used in this library, and never inferred from the set.
Unbounded intervals are assigned no length.

derivations.claim:
(Characterization.) Fix smooth vector fields $X,Y$. Evaluating the coordinate formula of [L1] on $X,Y$, $(\mathcal L_\xi g)(X,Y)=\xi^c\partial_cg_{ab}X^aY^b+g_{cb}\partial_a\xi^cX^aY^b+g_{ac}\partial_b\xi^cX^aY^b$. On the other hand, by [L2], $
abla_a\xi_b+
abla_b\xi_a=g_{bc}(\partial_a\xi^c+\Gamma^{c}{}_{ad}\xi^d)+g_{ac}(\partial_b\xi^c+\Gamma^{c}{}_{bd}\xi^d)=g_{bc}\partial_a\xi^c+g_{ac}\partial_b\xi^c+\xi^d(g_{bc}\Gamma^{c}{}_{ad}+g_{ac}\Gamma^{c}{}_{bd})$; metric compatibility in the form $\partial_dg_{ab}=g_{bc}\Gamma^{c}{}_{ad}+g_{ac}\Gamma^{c}{}_{bd}$ (which is the Christoffel formula of [L2]) makes the last term $\xi^d\partial_dg_{ab}$. Hence $(
abla_a\xi_b+
abla_b\xi_a)X^aY^b=(\mathcal L_\xi g)(X,Y)$ for all $X,Y$, and since $X,Y$ are arbitrary, $\mathcal L_\xi g$ vanishes exactly when the symmetrized derivative vanishes. This proves (a).

(The invariance identity.) Fix any compactly supported smooth $\xi$ with global flow $\Phi_v$ and let $G$ be as in (d). By [L8], $s\mapsto G(s,s)$ is differentiable at $0$ with derivative $\partial_uG(0,0)+\partial_vG(0,0)$; by (H4), $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ is constant in $s$, so this derivative vanishes. Substituting (H2) and (H3), $$0=0-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad q^{ab}=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}\big|_{v=0}.$$

(Contraction along geodesics.) Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ and $\xi$ Killing. By [L3], $ rac{d}{dt}g(\xi,\gamma')=g(D_t\xi,\gamma')+g(\xi,D_t\gamma')=g(D_t\xi,\gamma')$, and $D_t\xi$ is the restriction to $\gamma$ of $
abla_{\gamma'}\xi$. By (a), $g(
abla_{\gamma'}\xi,\gamma')=	frac12(
abla_a\xi_b+
abla_b\xi_a)\gamma'^a\gamma'^b=0$. Hence the derivative vanishes identically and the function is constant on $I$; this proves (b).

(Conserved current.) On $U$ put $J^a=T^{ab}\xi_b$. By [L2] and $
abla g^{-1}=0$, $
abla_aJ^a=(
abla_aT^{ab})\xi_b+T^{ab}
abla_a\xi_b$. The first term vanishes by hypothesis, and the second is $	frac12T^{ab}(
abla_a\xi_b+
abla_b\xi_a)=0$ because $T$ is symmetric and $\xi$ Killing, using (a). Hence $
abla_aJ^a=0$; the flux-balance assertion is clause (b) of [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] applied to this $J$.

(The inverse-metric variation.) By [L7], $(\Phi_v^*g)^{-1}=\Phi_v^*(g^{-1})$, so $q^{ab}=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*(g^{-1}))^{ab}|_{v=0}=(\mathcal L_\xi g^{-1})^{ab}$. Differentiating $g^{ac}(v)g_{cb}(v)=\delta^a{}_b$ for the family $g(v):=\Phi_v^*g$ with $\partial_vg_{cb}|_{v=0}=(\mathcal L_\xi g)_{cb}=
abla_c\xi_b+
abla_b\xi_c$ (step 1.1) gives $(\mathcal L_\xi g^{-1})^{ab}=-g^{ac}g^{bd}(\mathcal L_\xi g)_{cd}=-(
abla^a\xi^b+
abla^b\xi^a)$, where indices are raised with $g^{-1}$ by [L2].

(Vanishing of the divergence.) Fix a chart $(U,x)$; the hypotheses hold for every compactly supported smooth $\xi$ supported in $U$. Writing the last integral in the chart and putting $W_b:=\nabla^aT_{ab}$, a smooth covector field on $U$, step 3.1 gives $\int_UW_b\xi^bw\,d^4x=0$ for every such $\xi$, so $W=0$ on $U$ by [L5]; the integral-of-a-divergence identity in [L5] was already used through [L4]. Since every point lies in a chart, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$, which proves (d).
