clause (f): each displayed set of inequalities implies the corresponding condition — the converse sentences of steps 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1.

risk_review.notes: Read all eight steps. Constant Lambda and kappa>0 give conservation and the four-dimensional trace -S+4Lambda; variable Lambda gives kappa div T=dLambda, including disconnected locally constant branches. Corrected the overstrong any-metric nonconservation corollary: divergence is relative to the proposed metric. Rest-frame quadratic endpoint tests give WEC, NEC and SEC in both directions; closed future cone including zero gives DEC iff epsilon>=|p|, also at epsilon=p=0. Defined the dual covectors e^A rather than misusing coordinate dx^A in a pointwise frame. Replaced absence-of-postulate nonimplication with a complete local metric calculation for g=-dt^2+exp(2(t/L)^2) dx squared: epsilon=3H^2/kappa, p=-(2Hprime+3H^2)/kappa solve the direct field/fluid equations but at t=0 epsilon=0,p<0 violate all four conditions. This preserves the strongest nonimplication claim while allowing particular matter models to derive positivity.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the
sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] (so that its
charts that are oriented in that orientation have orientation-preserving
transition maps), and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection. This item
fixes the metric volume form, the flux of a current through oriented $3$-faces
and finite-chain charges. The orientation of $M$ is an independent datum: it is
not determined by the metric and not by the time orientation.

**(a) Metric volume density and volume form.** Let $(U,x)$ be an oriented
chart, with metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)). Define the **metric volume
density**

$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a strictly positive smooth function because $g_{ab}$ is smooth and
$g_p$ is nondegenerate. In the chart define the local $4$-form

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}:=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

with the exterior product of [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]] and the
coordinate covector fields of
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. That these local
forms agree on chart overlaps and therefore define one smooth nowhere-vanishing
$4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — is proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (a), together
with the reading statement of clause (b) there: in every oriented chart
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^3$, and on every positively
oriented $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ one has
$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1$.

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a
smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current
$3$-form** of $J$ is the contraction

$$\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

the interior product of the $4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $J$
([[def-interior-product-of-a-form-by-a-vector-field]]).

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-simplex` (differential-geometry track),
restated here so this page is self-contained — we mean a map
$\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ whose domain is the standard $k$-simplex
$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$
for which there exist an open set $O\subseteq A^k=\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\sum_it_i=1\}$
containing $\Delta^k$ and a smooth map $\bar\sigma:O\to M$ with
$\bar\sigma|_{\Delta^k}=\sigma$; the extension is not part of the simplex
data, and degenerate parametrizations are allowed. With the integration of
forms over such simplices
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]]), a **$3$-face** is
a smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$, and the **flux of $J$ through
$\sigma$** is the real number

$$\Phi_J(\sigma):=\int_\sigma\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

A **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes`, restated here —
is a finite formal real linear combination $\Sigma=\sum_i c_i\sigma_i$ of
smooth singular $k$-simplices. For such a $3$-chain the **flux of $J$ through
$\Sigma$** is defined additively,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma):=\sum_i c_i\,\Phi_J(\sigma_i),$$

a definition independent of the written expression for $\Sigma$, because a
finite formal sum is evaluated by adding the finitely many coefficients and
inserting a zero coefficient changes nothing. $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ is the **charge**
of the current $J$ assigned to $\Sigma$ when the model reads $J$ as a conserved
current; that reading belongs to the physical postulates and is not part of
this definition.

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace
$H\subseteq T_pM$ is **nondegenerate** for $g_p$ when the restriction of $g_p$
to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has
dimension $3$ and is nondegenerate at $\sigma(t)$, and **non-null** when this holds at every
parameter point. For a non-null face the **unit normal** $\nu$ at that point is
the unique vector of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$ with $\nu\in H^\perp$,
$g(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $(\nu,\sigma_*\partial_1,\sigma_*\partial_2,
\sigma_*\partial_3)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$; its
existence, uniqueness and its sign $\varepsilon:=g(\nu,\nu)$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c), together
with the density identity of clause (c) used to read $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ on
such a face. Rank-deficient faces and rank-three faces with degenerate induced
metric are not assigned a unit normal; their flux is defined
by the $3$-form $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ itself, as in clause (b).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose underlying manifold carries an
orientation ([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), and let
$w$ and the local forms $\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}$ be as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a).

**(a) Chart independence.** Let $(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be oriented charts with
$x=\varphi\circ y$ on the overlap of their domains, where $\varphi$ is the
smooth transition map; write $g_{ab}$ and $g'_{ab}$ for the metric components
in the two charts and $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$,
$w'=\sqrt{|\det(g'_{ab})|}$. Then

$$\det(g'_{ab})=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)^{2}\det\bigl(g_{ab}\circ\varphi\bigr),\qquad w'=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)\,(w\circ\varphi),$$

and the local forms agree on the overlap,

$$\varphi^{*}\bigl(w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\bigr)=w'\,dy^0\wedge dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3 .$$

Consequently there is a unique smooth nowhere-vanishing $4$-form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — whose restriction to the
domain of every oriented chart $(U,x)$ is $w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge
dx^3$; it is a smooth section with nowhere-zero values and positive on the
given orientation.

**(b) Value on orthonormal frames.** For every $p\in M$ and every positively
oriented ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ with
$g_p(e_A,e_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$,

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1 .$$

**(c) Non-null hyperplanes: normal and density.** Let $p\in M$, let
$H\subseteq T_pM$ be a $3$-dimensional subspace that is nondegenerate for
$g_p$, and let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be an ordered basis of $H$. Then $H^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate and $H=(H^{\perp})^{\perp}$. Let
$u\in H^{\perp}\setminus\{0\}$ and write $\nu:=u/\sqrt{|g_p(u,u)|}$, so that
$\varepsilon:=g_p(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,1\}$. If $\delta\in\{-1,1\}$ is the sign for
which $(\delta\nu,v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is a positively oriented basis of $T_pM$, then
$\nu^{*}:=\delta\nu$ is the **unit normal to $H$ adapted to the ordered basis**
$(v_1,v_2,v_3)$; it satisfies $g_p(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})=\varepsilon$,
$g_p(\nu^{*},h)=0$ for every $h\in H$, and it is the unique vector with these
two properties for which $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively oriented.
Moreover

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)=\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_p(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|}.$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $X:M\to TM$ be a smooth section of the tangent bundle, that is, a smooth
vector field on $M$, and let $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$. The **interior product**
$\iota_X\omega\in\Omega^{k-1}(M)$ is defined pointwise by

$$ (\iota_X\omega)_p:=\iota_{X_p}\omega_p. $$

For $k=0$, adopt the formal convention $\Omega^{-1}(M):=\{0\}$ and set
$\iota_X\omega:=0$.

This pointwise field is smooth. Indeed, in local coordinates write
$X=\sum_jX^j\partial_j$ and expand $\omega$ in the smooth frame $dx^I$ as in
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. The coefficients
of $\iota_X\omega$ are signed finite sums of products $X^j\omega_I$, and are
therefore smooth.

Let $\alpha\in\Omega^k(M)$ and $\beta\in\Omega^\ell(M)$. Their **wedge product**
is the differential form defined pointwise by

$$ (\alpha\wedge\beta)_p:=\alpha_p\wedge\beta_p\in\operatorname{Alt}^{k+\ell}(T_pM). $$

The next proposition verifies that this pointwise field is smooth.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose underlying manifold carries an
orientation ([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), and let
$w$ and the local forms $\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}$ be as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a).

**(a) Chart independence.** Let $(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be oriented charts with
$x=\varphi\circ y$ on the overlap of their domains, where $\varphi$ is the
smooth transition map; write $g_{ab}$ and $g'_{ab}$ for the metric components
in the two charts and $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$,
$w'=\sqrt{|\det(g'_{ab})|}$. Then

$$\det(g'_{ab})=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)^{2}\det\bigl(g_{ab}\circ\varphi\bigr),\qquad w'=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)\,(w\circ\varphi),$$

and the local forms agree on the overlap,

$$\varphi^{*}\bigl(w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\bigr)=w'\,dy^0\wedge dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3 .$$

Consequently there is a unique smooth nowhere-vanishing $4$-form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — whose restriction to the
domain of every oriented chart $(U,x)$ is $w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge
dx^3$; it is a smooth section with nowhere-zero values and positive on the
given orientation.

**(b) Value on orthonormal frames.** For every $p\in M$ and every positively
oriented ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ with
$g_p(e_A,e_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$,

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1 .$$

**(c) Non-null hyperplanes: normal and density.** Let $p\in M$, let
$H\subseteq T_pM$ be a $3$-dimensional subspace that is nondegenerate for
$g_p$, and let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be an ordered basis of $H$. Then $H^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate and $H=(H^{\perp})^{\perp}$. Let
$u\in H^{\perp}\setminus\{0\}$ and write $\nu:=u/\sqrt{|g_p(u,u)|}$, so that
$\varepsilon:=g_p(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,1\}$. If $\delta\in\{-1,1\}$ is the sign for
which $(\delta\nu,v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is a positively oriented basis of $T_pM$, then
$\nu^{*}:=\delta\nu$ is the **unit normal to $H$ adapted to the ordered basis**
$(v_1,v_2,v_3)$; it satisfies $g_p(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})=\varepsilon$,
$g_p(\nu^{*},h)=0$ for every $h\in H$, and it is the unique vector with these
two properties for which $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively oriented.
Moreover

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)=\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_p(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|}.$$

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ and $B\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ be nondegenerate closed rectangles, and let $f:A\times B\to\mathbb R$ be Riemann integrable. Then the four lower and upper section-integral functions of [[def-sections-and-iterated-riemann-integrals]] are Riemann integrable and
$$\int_A\ell_B=\int_Au_B=\int_{A\times B}f=\int_B\ell_A=\int_Bu_A.$$

If the $B$-sections are integrable outside a content-zero set $N\subseteq A$, every bounded exceptionally completed function $h$ with $h(x)=\int_Bf_x$ for $x\notin N$ is integrable and
$$\int_{A\times B}f=\int_Ah.$$
The same assertion holds with the coordinate blocks exchanged. In particular, when every section in an order is integrable, the ordinary iterated integral in that order exists and equals the multiple integral. The theorem does not assert that every section of an integrable function is integrable.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Let $\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ be a smooth singular simplex and let $\omega$ be a smooth $k$-form on an open neighbourhood of its image in $M$. For $k\ge1$ put
$$T_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^k:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j\le1\},\qquad a(x)=v_0+\sum_{j=1}^kx_j(v_j-v_0).$$
Take a smooth extension $\bar\sigma$ near $\Delta^k$, restrict its domain so that $\omega$ is defined on its image, and write $a^*\bar\sigma^*\omega=f(x)\,dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_k$. Define
$$\int_\sigma\omega:=\int_{T_k}f(x)\,dx.$$
The right side is the Jordan-set Riemann integral. In degree zero define $\int_\sigma\omega=\omega(\sigma(v_0))$. This fixes the positive point convention. Reversing the domain orientation negates the integral. Independence of other positive affine coordinates is the forward justification [[lem-simplex-integrals-are-independent-of-affine-coordinate-identification]].

derivations.claim: (Density and volume form.) Since $g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ is constant, $w=\sqrt{|\det g|}=\sqrt{|-1|}=1$, and [L1] gives $\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. Evaluating on the coordinate frame, $\mathrm{vol}_g(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)=w\det(\delta^a{}_b)=1$.

(Connection and divergence.) The Christoffel symbols of the constant metric vanish: $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})=0$. By [L2], $\nabla$ is the coordinate connection, so for $J=x^1\partial_1$ (components $J^0=0$, $J^1=x^1$, $J^2=J^3=0$) the divergence is $\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_0 0+\partial_1x^1+\partial_2 0+\partial_3 0=1$.

(Current form and its derivative.) By [L3], $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g=(-1)^1J^1dx^0\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3=-x^1dx^0\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. Differentiating by [L4], $d(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g)=-\partial_1x^1\,dx^1\wedge dx^0\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3=\mathrm{vol}_g$, which equals $(\nabla_aJ^a)\mathrm{vol}_g$ by step 1.2.

(Two flux orientations.) On the affine simplex $\sigma_-$, the ordered velocities are $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=(\partial_0,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ and their Gram matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1)$, so its determinant is $-1$ and the induced density is $1$. The ambient ordered basis $(\partial_1,\partial_0,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ is negatively oriented; therefore the adapted normal is $
u_-^{*}=-\partial_1$. The face is non-null, $\varepsilon=1$, and $\varepsilon g(J_0,
u_-^{*})=-1$. Hence $\sigma_-^*(\iota_{J_0}\mathrm{vol}_g)=-dt_1\wedge dt_2\wedge dt_3$ and $\Phi_{J_0}(\sigma_-)=-1/6$. On $\sigma_+$, the ordered velocities are $(\partial_2,\partial_0,\partial_3)$ with the same Gram determinant $-1$ and density $1$; now $(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_0,\partial_3)$ is positively oriented, so $
u_+^{*}=+\partial_1$ and $\varepsilon g(J_0,
u_+^{*})=1$. Thus $\sigma_+^*(\iota_{J_0}\mathrm{vol}_g)=dt_1\wedge dt_2\wedge dt_3$ and $\Phi_{J_0}(\sigma_+)=1/6$, since the coordinate volume of $\Delta^3$ is $1/6$. This verifies clause 4 with consistent orientations and the induced area densities.

boundaries.reason: The example evaluates fixed data on four-dimensional space in the identity chart; no empty-domain or empty-chain instance is claimed.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.2: the field x^1 partial_1 vanishes on the hyperplane where the first coordinate is zero, and its divergence is still one there; step 2.1 differentiates the resulting form.
step 1.1: the volume form evaluates to one on the coordinate frame, the normalization fixed in the metric-volume definition.

boundaries.reason: The flat metric is nondegenerate and the two faces displayed are non-null; null or degenerate simplices are outside this example.
The computations are pointwise and chart-local; no integral over a chain or its boundary is performed.
The chart, the orientation and the vector fields are explicitly fixed; nothing is selected.
The clauses record identities and a sign convention, not an equivalence.
No converse is asserted about arbitrary fields realizing these coordinate expressions.

risk_review.notes: Checked all four steps: w=1 and Gamma=0; x1 partial_1 has divergence 1 and current form -x1 dx0 wedge dx2 wedge dx3 whose derivative is vol_g. Affine parameter orientations yield normals -partial_1 and +partial_1 and fluxes -1/6,+1/6 for constant J0=partial_1. Both face Gram determinants are -1 and rank three, so the repaired non-null predicate is satisfied. No arbitrary or unbounded-region integration.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the
sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] (so that its
charts that are oriented in that orientation have orientation-preserving
transition maps), and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection. This item
fixes the metric volume form, the flux of a current through oriented $3$-faces
and finite-chain charges. The orientation of $M$ is an independent datum: it is
not determined by the metric and not by the time orientation.

**(a) Metric volume density and volume form.** Let $(U,x)$ be an oriented
chart, with metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)). Define the **metric volume
density**

$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a strictly positive smooth function because $g_{ab}$ is smooth and
$g_p$ is nondegenerate. In the chart define the local $4$-form

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}:=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

with the exterior product of [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]] and the
coordinate covector fields of
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. That these local
forms agree on chart overlaps and therefore define one smooth nowhere-vanishing
$4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — is proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (a), together
with the reading statement of clause (b) there: in every oriented chart
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^3$, and on every positively
oriented $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ one has
$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1$.

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a
smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current
$3$-form** of $J$ is the contraction

$$\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

the interior product of the $4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $J$
([[def-interior-product-of-a-form-by-a-vector-field]]).

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-simplex` (differential-geometry track),
restated here so this page is self-contained — we mean a map
$\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ whose domain is the standard $k$-simplex
$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$
for which there exist an open set $O\subseteq A^k=\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\sum_it_i=1\}$
containing $\Delta^k$ and a smooth map $\bar\sigma:O\to M$ with
$\bar\sigma|_{\Delta^k}=\sigma$; the extension is not part of the simplex
data, and degenerate parametrizations are allowed. With the integration of
forms over such simplices
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]]), a **$3$-face** is
a smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$, and the **flux of $J$ through
$\sigma$** is the real number

$$\Phi_J(\sigma):=\int_\sigma\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

A **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes`, restated here —
is a finite formal real linear combination $\Sigma=\sum_i c_i\sigma_i$ of
smooth singular $k$-simplices. For such a $3$-chain the **flux of $J$ through
$\Sigma$** is defined additively,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma):=\sum_i c_i\,\Phi_J(\sigma_i),$$

a definition independent of the written expression for $\Sigma$, because a
finite formal sum is evaluated by adding the finitely many coefficients and
inserting a zero coefficient changes nothing. $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ is the **charge**
of the current $J$ assigned to $\Sigma$ when the model reads $J$ as a conserved
current; that reading belongs to the physical postulates and is not part of
this definition.

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace
$H\subseteq T_pM$ is **nondegenerate** for $g_p$ when the restriction of $g_p$
to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has
dimension $3$ and is nondegenerate at $\sigma(t)$, and **non-null** when this holds at every
parameter point. For a non-null face the **unit normal** $\nu$ at that point is
the unique vector of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$ with $\nu\in H^\perp$,
$g(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $(\nu,\sigma_*\partial_1,\sigma_*\partial_2,
\sigma_*\partial_3)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$; its
existence, uniqueness and its sign $\varepsilon:=g(\nu,\nu)$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c), together
with the density identity of clause (c) used to read $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ on
such a face. Rank-deficient faces and rank-three faces with degenerate induced
metric are not assigned a unit normal; their flux is defined
by the $3$-form $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ itself, as in clause (b).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $X:M\to TM$ be a smooth section of the tangent bundle, that is, a smooth
vector field on $M$, and let $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$. The **interior product**
$\iota_X\omega\in\Omega^{k-1}(M)$ is defined pointwise by

$$ (\iota_X\omega)_p:=\iota_{X_p}\omega_p. $$

For $k=0$, adopt the formal convention $\Omega^{-1}(M):=\{0\}$ and set
$\iota_X\omega:=0$.

This pointwise field is smooth. Indeed, in local coordinates write
$X=\sum_jX^j\partial_j$ and expand $\omega$ in the smooth frame $dx^I$ as in
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. The coefficients
of $\iota_X\omega$ are signed finite sums of products $X^j\omega_I$, and are
therefore smooth.

Let $\alpha\in\Omega^k(M)$ and $\beta\in\Omega^\ell(M)$. Their **wedge product**
is the differential form defined pointwise by

$$ (\alpha\wedge\beta)_p:=\alpha_p\wedge\beta_p\in\operatorname{Alt}^{k+\ell}(T_pM). $$

The next proposition verifies that this pointwise field is smooth.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose underlying manifold carries an
orientation ([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), and let
$w$ and the local forms $\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}$ be as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a).

**(a) Chart independence.** Let $(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be oriented charts with
$x=\varphi\circ y$ on the overlap of their domains, where $\varphi$ is the
smooth transition map; write $g_{ab}$ and $g'_{ab}$ for the metric components
in the two charts and $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$,
$w'=\sqrt{|\det(g'_{ab})|}$. Then

$$\det(g'_{ab})=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)^{2}\det\bigl(g_{ab}\circ\varphi\bigr),\qquad w'=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)\,(w\circ\varphi),$$

and the local forms agree on the overlap,

$$\varphi^{*}\bigl(w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\bigr)=w'\,dy^0\wedge dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3 .$$

Consequently there is a unique smooth nowhere-vanishing $4$-form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — whose restriction to the
domain of every oriented chart $(U,x)$ is $w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge
dx^3$; it is a smooth section with nowhere-zero values and positive on the
given orientation.

**(b) Value on orthonormal frames.** For every $p\in M$ and every positively
oriented ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ with
$g_p(e_A,e_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$,

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1 .$$

**(c) Non-null hyperplanes: normal and density.** Let $p\in M$, let
$H\subseteq T_pM$ be a $3$-dimensional subspace that is nondegenerate for
$g_p$, and let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be an ordered basis of $H$. Then $H^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate and $H=(H^{\perp})^{\perp}$. Let
$u\in H^{\perp}\setminus\{0\}$ and write $\nu:=u/\sqrt{|g_p(u,u)|}$, so that
$\varepsilon:=g_p(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,1\}$. If $\delta\in\{-1,1\}$ is the sign for
which $(\delta\nu,v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is a positively oriented basis of $T_pM$, then
$\nu^{*}:=\delta\nu$ is the **unit normal to $H$ adapted to the ordered basis**
$(v_1,v_2,v_3)$; it satisfies $g_p(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})=\varepsilon$,
$g_p(\nu^{*},h)=0$ for every $h\in H$, and it is the unique vector with these
two properties for which $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively oriented.
Moreover

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)=\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_p(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|}.$$

derivations.claim: (Divergence.) By [L1], $\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a=\partial_0 0+\partial_1 0+\partial_2x^1+\partial_3 0=0$.

(Current form.) By [L2] and $J^2=x^1$, $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g=x^1dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^3$. Its exterior derivative is $\partial_1x^1\,dx^1\wedge dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^3=0$, because $dx^1$ occurs twice; consistently, [L3] and step 1.1 give $d(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$.

(Flux densities.) At a point of a face with adapted unit normal $
u^{*}=\partial_2$ (so $\varepsilon=g(\partial_2,\partial_2)=1$ and $\sqrt{|\det(g(v_i,v_j))|}=1$ for a coordinate face), [L4] gives the flux density $g(J,\partial_2)=g(x^1\partial_2,\partial_2)=x^1$; for $
u^{*}=-\partial_2$ it is $-x^1$. For $
u^{*}=\pm\partial_1$, $g(J,\pm\partial_1)=0$; for $
u^{*}=\pm\partial_0$, $g(J,\pm\partial_0)=0$. This is the displayed list of values. Since $x^1
eq0$ on the open set $\{x^1
eq0\}$, the flux density through the faces normal to $\partial_2$ is nonzero there although the divergence of $J$ vanishes identically, which completes the verification.

boundaries.reason: An explicit field on four-dimensional space is presented; no empty-chain or empty-region claim is made.

boundaries.evidence: steps 1.1 and 2.1: both the divergence and the exterior derivative of the current form vanish; step 3.1 shows the flux density vanishes for the normals along the first and zeroth directions.
step 3.1: the flux densities through the two faces normal to the second coordinate direction are opposite values of the same magnitude, fixed by the orientation sign.

boundaries.reason: The faces displayed are coordinate faces with nondegenerate tangent span, and null faces lie outside the face-formula hypotheses.
Flux densities are evaluated pointwise; the example integrates nothing and evaluates no boundary value.
The field and the four coordinate normals are explicitly given; no selection occurs.
The example illustrates the balance identity rather than an equivalence.
No converse is asserted about fields whose face fluxes vanish.

risk_review.notes: Read all three steps: J=x1 partial_2 has divergence zero and insertion sign (-1)^2 gives x1 dx0 wedge dx1 wedge dx3; its exterior derivative repeats dx1 and vanishes. For coordinate velocity bases, adapted normals +/-partial_2 give +/-x1 while +/-partial_0 and +/-partial_1 give zero. At x1=0 the density is zero; elsewhere it is nonzero. Reader title/notation repair correctly distinguishes pointwise face-flux density from an unexhibited integrated side-chain flux; the remark preserves the actual finite-chain balance theorem. No empirical assertion.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The parameter $\rho$ is the coefficient in the unit-normalized tensor of
clause (b); this mathematical definition assigns it no physical unit. In the
framework's SI stress-energy reading it is the **rest energy density**
$\varepsilon:=\rho$, in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The **rest-mass
density** is instead $\rho_m:=\varepsilon/c^2$, in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the physical four-velocity is
$U:=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Thus the same tensor is
$T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b=\rho_m U^aU^b$. A purely mathematical or
$c=1$ convention may rescale the density coefficient; interpreting $\rho$
as an SI mass density while keeping the unit tangent $u$ would require the
explicit tensor $c^2\rho\,u\otimes u$. Physical realizations and readings
are adopted by the matter postulate, not deduced here.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** has the
smooth symmetric contravariant components and their covariant lowering

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

Let $(M,\mathcal S)$ be a smooth $n$-manifold and let $U\subseteq M$ be open,
carrying the subspace topology. Then $U$ is a topological $n$-manifold. For
every smooth atlas $\mathcal A$ with $[\mathcal A]=\mathcal S$, the family of
restricted charts

$$\mathcal A|_U:=\bigl\{\,\bigl(V\cap U,\ \varphi|_{V\cap U}\bigr):(V,\varphi)\in\mathcal A\,\bigr\}.$$

is a smooth atlas on $U$, and the maximal atlas it generates is independent of
the presenting atlas $\mathcal A$: it depends only on the structure
$\mathcal S$. This maximal atlas is the **restricted smooth structure** of $U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u)$ be a dust model on $U$, and let
$T_{ab}:=\rho u_a u_b$ be its derived tensor
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$, with derived tensor $T_{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n_an_b+p g_{ab}$,
comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

derivations.claim: (The unit field is ${\partial_0}$.) The field $u=\partial_0$ has constant components $(1,0,0,0)$, is smooth, satisfies $g(u,u)=-1$ and $g(u,N)=-1<0$, so it is a future-directed unit timelike field by [L1].

(Conserved time-independent density.) Let $ho>0$ be smooth with $\partial_0ho=0$. By [L3], $
abla_a(ho u^a)=\partial_0ho=0$ and $u^a
abla_au^b=\partial_0(\delta^b{}_0)=0$: the dust system holds, so by [L2] $
abla^aT_{ab}=0$. This is clause 1.

(Time-dependent density.) Let $ho(t,x)=1+t$, positive on the open set $U=\{x^0>-1\}$, and restrict $u$ to $U$; both restrictions are smooth on $U$, and $u|_U$ remains future-directed, unit and timelike. By [L3] applied on $U$, $
abla_a(ho u^a)=\partial_0ho=1
eq0$, so the dust system fails; directly, $T^{ab}=(1+t)\delta^a{}_0\delta^b{}_0$ and $
abla_aT^{ab}=\partial_0(1+t)\delta^{0b}=\delta^{0b}$, and lowering the free index gives $
abla^aT_{ab}=g_{bc}
abla_aT^{ac}=-\delta^0{}_b$, which is nonzero on $U$. This is clause 2, and it shows that the equivalence of [L2] is not vacuous.

boundaries.reason: The models are defined on four-dimensional space and on the open half-space with positive time, neither of which is empty.

boundaries.evidence: step 2.1: the static family has vanishing divergence, the zero side of the dichotomy; step 3.1 exhibits the nonzero divergence of the time-dependent family.
step 1.1: the unit field has the single nonvanishing component one and its normalization is fixed by the metric pairing.

boundaries.reason: The unit field is timelike and the density is strictly positive on its domain, so no null or degenerate congruence is treated.

boundaries.evidence: step 3.1: the restriction to the open half-space keeps the density positive in the interior; the boundary value of time is never used.

boundaries.reason: The fields are explicitly given and the restriction to the half-space selects nothing.
The example instantiates the cited equivalence but does not restate or prove it.
No converse direction is asserted here; the equivalence lives in the cited proposition.

risk_review.notes: All three steps checked: u=partial_0 is future unit timelike; stationary positive rho gives both dust equations and conservation. For rho=1+x0, only x0>-1 is a dust domain, continuity fails with derivative 1 and lowering the free index gives -delta^0_b. Corrected “homogeneous” in the remark because stationary rho may vary spatially. It is a prescribed model computation, without a flat Einstein solution or empirical assertion.
